1.why: The interface uses a clean sans-serif face at a comfortable size with reasonable line spacing in headings, body copy and labels, though the monospace secret and small grey log text are tighter than ideal.

2.why: No italics or all-caps are used anywhere, and all instructional text appears as one- or two-line sentences rather than dense paragraphs.

3.why: All screenshots are desktop-width (1280px) with a fixed centred card, so mobile rendering cannot be confirmed, and the 32-character secret string risks overflow on a narrow phone screen.

4.why: Instructions such as 'Enter your registered details to begin MFA enrolment' and 'Use an authenticator app for payment approvals' are short and plain, though 'Choose manual entry and enter this setup secret' assumes some prior knowledge.

5.why: No sample or placeholder is shown for the six-digit authenticator code field; only the login fields contain pre-filled values, and no format example is given for the expected input.

6.why: Every screen contains only brief one-line instructions, and nothing requires reading a long block of text before proceeding.

7.why: The 32-character setup secret is displayed in a plain read-only box with no copy button or copy affordance, so it must be manually transcribed.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent is offered at all; the setup screen explicitly directs the user to 'Choose manual entry' as the only path.

9.why: There is no visible indication of autofill or password-manager support (no autocomplete/one-time-code affordances), and the OTP field is a bare text input.

10.why: The primary blue button is visually dominant on each screen, but there is no step indicator or progress marker showing which stage of enrolment the user is on.

11.why: Each screen presents a single primary action (Verify and continue, Set up authenticator app, Confirm code), with only a secondary 'Log out' alongside it.

12.why: Feedback is confined to a technical 'Logs' panel with developer-oriented lines like 'Authenticator provisioning created. Test values were written to the browser console.', and no plain statement of what happened or what comes next is given.

13.why: The user can re-enter the code after failure, but there is no reveal/hide toggle, no way to re-request or regenerate the secret, and no backup recovery codes screen appears at all.

14.why: The error 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.' avoids blaming the user but does not say what was wrong (e.g. expired or mistyped code) or how to fix it.

15.why: The screen relies on a time-bound TOTP with no timer, no statement about how long the code is valid, and no reassurance that there is generous time to read or enter it.
